subject: Russia Hits Three Kyiv Bridges. Venezuela Signs a US Military Pact. Asia Tech Stocks Slide.
preview_text: Kyiv under fire, a new Caracas alliance, an AI sell-off, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
description: Russia strikes three Kyiv bridges, Venezuela signs a military deal with the US and SoftBank leads an Asian tech sell-off.
contents_extra: BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Russia Hits Three Kyiv Bridges in One of the War's Largest Air Attacks
paragraphs: The BBC reports ballistic missiles hit three bridges over the Dnipro River in Kyiv overnight. The BBC says eight people were killed, six of them in the capital. Ukraine's air force says Russia launched almost 100 missiles and around 400 drones. The BBC says the attack came days after Ukraine damaged the Crimean Bridge.

Politico reports Poland's prime minister Donald Tusk was briefed on a violation of Polish airspace. Rzeszow airport suspended flights, the outlet says. Politico cites lower early tolls, including at least five dead. Kyiv's mayor Vitali Klitschko urged residents not to drive into the city. Putin had vowed a response far more painful than Ukraine's bridge strike.

stories.title: Venezuela Signs a Military Cooperation Deal With the United States
paragraphs: The BBC reports Venezuela's interim government signed a military cooperation agreement with US defence secretary Pete Hegseth. The deal was signed on Wednesday in Caracas. Few details have been released, the BBC says. Military ties were cut in 2005 by Hugo Chavez. Interim President Delcy Rodriguez said the deal would help confront common threats.

The Guardian reports Hegseth used the visit to boast of Nicolas Maduro's capture by US forces. Maduro was seized on Jan. 3 and is in custody in New York. He and his wife deny the charges, the BBC says. Hegseth said he looks forward to unlocking Venezuela's resources together.

stories.title: SoftBank Leads an AI Sell-Off Across Asia's Tech Stocks
paragraphs: CNBC reports SoftBank Group shares closed 14.48% lower on Friday in Tokyo. It was the stock's worst day since August 2024. CNBC says the sell-off swept Asian tech stocks after Anthropic's market debut. South Korea's Kospi ended 5.21% lower, while TSMC closed 4.76% lower in Taiwan.

CNBC reports Anthropic was down 6.37% in premarket trading at 5 a.m. ET on Friday. Nvidia was down 2.67% and AMD fell 5.43% at that time. Anthropic had closed at $97.17 on Thursday after its debut. US markets open at 9:30 a.m. ET.

deep_dive.title: After Eight Years in Space, BepiColombo Prepares to Orbit Mercury
paragraphs: The BBC reports the BepiColombo spacecraft is about to get into orbit around Mercury. It has travelled almost six billion miles over eight years. The mission is a collaboration between the European and Japanese space agencies. It launched from French Guiana in 2018. A propulsion problem added a year to the journey, the BBC says.

The Guardian reports flight controllers will fire the thrusters on Saturday to send it into orbit. It would become only the second mission to circle the planet. The paper puts the mission's cost at EUR 1.6bn. Scientists hope to learn why Mercury has a magnetic field and an unusually large core.

ESA says four thrusters will slow the spacecraft as it approaches Mercury's south pole. It will first enter an elliptical orbit of 590 by 11,640 km. The two orbiters are due to separate on Dec. 9-10. Science operations for both spacecraft are set to begin in April 2027, ESA says.

The BBC says the final manoeuvre is perilous, a 37-minute turn to be grabbed by gravity. If anything goes wrong, the craft could hurtle past Mercury. Only two Nasa missions have visited before. The BBC says scientists also want to explain ice in polar craters and strange young hollows on the surface.

trivia.question: How long is a single day on Mercury, measured in Earth days, according to the BBC?
trivia.explanation: The answer is 59. The BBC reports a Mercury year lasts just 88 Earth days but a day lasts 59.

World view: Houthi forces besiege Yemen's city of Taiz, The BBC reports officials say attacks killed over 140 civilians since August.
A US envoy says Russia may accept guarantees, CNBC reports Jared Kushner said Russia is comfortable with an Article 5-like idea.
A US group wins Kenya's Mrima Hill mining tender, The BBC reports rival bidders intend to challenge the selection.
Need to know: Nigeria's president moves to decriminalise attempted suicide, The BBC reports Bola Tinubu proposed medical support instead of prosecution.
Women protest at an Iraqi university over male teachers, The Guardian reports up to 400 women protested at Al-Qadisiyah University.
China warns citizens about off-season climbs of Mount Fuji, The BBC reports a missing hiker's family offered a large reward.
Money & markets: The race for the next UN chief faces a key vote, The Guardian reports a Security Council straw poll is likely on Friday.
Japan's core inflation rises to 2.2% in October, CNBC reports the figure was below the 2.3% economists expected.
Iceland's Blue Lagoon begins trading on Friday, CNBC reports the offering raised roughly 14.3 billion kronur.
Future frontiers: Europe resists new climate cash pledges for Africa, The BBC reports Africa wants adaptation finance tripled by 2035.
An Australian data center firm will avoid sites near homes, The Guardian reports NextDC changed course after a Melbourne backlash.
India tests the UK trade deal over Scotch whisky, CNBC cites Reuters reporting of a planned 162.5% duty on bulk Scotch.
The score: Australia stun Argentina at the U17 World Cup, The Guardian reports the Joeys won 2-0 in their opener.
F1 nears a V8 engine deal for 2030, BBC Sport reports Zak Brown cited an agreement in principle.
Magnus Carlsen's slump threatens his world No 1 spot, The Guardian reports a run of 10 winless games in Budapest.
Life & culture: GTA 6 sales are estimated to top $2.3 billion, The BBC cites Sensor Tower estimates of more than 24.5 million units.
Airbnb's new house rules come into force, The BBC reports hosts should not normally ask guests to wash up.
The Netherlands edge Scotland in a cricket thriller, BBC Sport reports the Dutch won by seven wickets.
